chunks: "I assume the ground will move and design so the system doesn't care. There are four layers to that.

First, signalling: on anything that leaves a board or crosses a noisy area, I use differential links like RS-485, CAN or LVDS, where the receiver only looks at the difference between the two wires and ignores a ground offset of volts.
When grounds can't be tied together at all, or voltages are large, I use galvanic isolation with a digital isolator or optocoupler, so there's no path for the offset to matter.
Second, measurements: I make them differential or ratiometric.
For example, a bridge sensor measured by an ADC that uses the same excitation as its reference, with a Kelvin connection at the sensor, so supply and ground shifts cancel in the ratio.
Third, margin and filtering: Schmitt-trigger inputs, slower edges, RC filters on slow signals, and sampling the ADC away from switching edges.
Fourth, recovery: CRC and retry on communications, watchdogs, brown-out resets and state that comes back safely, so a disturbance causes a retry instead of a crash.
And I put TVS and clamp parts right at the connector, with a short low-impedance path to ground, so a big event doesn't flow through the sensitive circuits."
